title: Canonical adjunction-transpose projection identity on resolving pairs
statement: Under the ringed-site, exact-adjunction, ordinary/cochain open tensor data and normalized restriction-comparison hypotheses of [def-sf-open-tensor-cochain-data] and [def-sf-open-tensor-representative-data], fix one-flat comparison families ambientModel and openModel which agree with the simultaneous K-flat models T and T′. For flat-term K-flat complexes C on the open site and P on the ambient site, the canonical projection mate (the adjoint transpose of tensor(unit,identity) followed by the inverse restriction comparison) satisfies the displayed localized chain projection equation. This is a calculation on resolving pairs, not an assertion for arbitrary unnormalized comparison families or arbitrary C.

proof.text: Construct the natural ordinary projection isomorphism tensorLeft(F(M)) ≅ G ⋙ tensorLeft(M) ⋙ F from D.ordinaryNaturality. Site-flatness gives categorical tensor exactness by flat_to_cat, and the site tensor comparison and symmetry return flatness of F(M). For a K-flat C and acyclic Z, exact G preserves acyclicity; apply hC, swap factors, apply exact F, and transport acyclicity through D.chain and the Koszul swap. This proves F(C) K-flat and its terms flat. D.pullFlat and restrictionModel.kflat give the corresponding properties on the restriction side.

Prove the adjunct of D.chain(C,P).inv equals totalTensor(unit,identity) followed by restrictionModel.chain(F(C),P). Apply cochain-map extensionality and total-coproduct summand extensionality. Naturality of the ordinary adjunction unit moves the summand insertion across it. D.summand, cancellation of the ordinary and chain isomorphisms, D.ordinaryInverse, hordinary, and restrictionModel.summand identify the two resulting summand maps.

The localized hom-equivalence sends F.factors.hom followed by Q.map(D.chain.inv) to Q.map of the cochain adjunct followed by G.factors.inv. Derive this from localization_unit_app and naturality of the exact-functor factorization. Apply restrictionModel.derived on F(C),P, cancelling the factorization and tensor-model isomorphisms. Naturality of T′.comparison at the cochain unit and naturality of restriction.inv, together with the localized unit formula, identify this adjunct with that of the canonicalProjectionMate after the open comparison. Injectivity of the hom-equivalence gives the inverse chain square. Precompose with Q.map(D.chain.hom) and F.factors.inv and cancel. Finally ambientBoth and openBoth identify the supplied one-flat comparisons with the simultaneous comparisons.

lean.statement:
theorem openTensorProjection_mate_canonical
    (D : OpenTensorCochainData.{c, v, r} J R J' R' F G adj H sectionPull)
    (restriction : A.tensor ⋙ G.mapDerivedCategory ≅
      (G.mapDerivedCategory.prod G.mapDerivedCategory) ⋙ A'.tensor)
    (restrictionModel : TensorComparisonModel.{c, v, r} J J' R R' G A A' T T' restriction)
    (hordinary : restrictionModel.ordinary = D.pullTensor)
    (ambientModel : RingedDerivedTensorComparison.{c, v, r, (max c v r) + 1} J R A)
    (ambientBoth : RingedDerivedTensorBothModel.{c, v, r, (max c v r) + 1}
      J R A T ambientModel)
    (openModel : RingedDerivedTensorComparison.{c, v, r, (max c v r) + 1} J' R' A')
    (openBoth : RingedDerivedTensorBothModel.{c, v, r, (max c v r) + 1}
      J' R' A' T' openModel)
    (C : CochainComplex (SemilinearSections.Mod.{c, v, max c v r} J' R') ℤ)
    (P : CochainComplex (SemilinearSections.Mod.{c, v, max c v r} J R) ℤ)
    (hC : CochainComplex.IsKFlatIndependentCoefficients (J := J') (R := R') C)
    (flatC : flatTerms.{c, v, r} J' R' C)
    (hP : CochainComplex.IsKFlatIndependentCoefficients (J := J) (R := R) P)
    (flatP : flatTerms.{c, v, r} J R P) :
      DerivedCategory.Q.map (D.chain C P).hom ≫
        F.mapDerivedCategoryFactors.inv.app ((totalTensor.{c, v, r} J' R').obj
          (C, (G.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P)) ≫
        F.mapDerivedCategory.map ((openModel C ((G.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P)
          (Or.inr (restrictionModel.kflat P hP flatP))).hom) ≫
        F.mapDerivedCategory.map (A'.tensor.map
          (Prod.mkHom (𝟙 _) (G.mapDerivedCategoryFactors.inv.app P))) ≫
        (canonicalProjectionMate A.tensor A'.tensor F.mapDerivedCategory
          G.mapDerivedCategory
          (SheafOfModules.OpenTensorNormalization.exactDerivedAdjunction adj)
          restriction).app (DerivedCategory.Q.obj C, DerivedCategory.Q.obj P) =
    (ambientModel ((F.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj C) P (Or.inr hP)).hom ≫
        A.tensor.map (Prod.mkHom (F.mapDerivedCategoryFactors.inv.app C) (𝟙 _))

statement_change.old_statement: Under the same ringed-site, tensor-comparison, and cochain hypotheses as the resolving-pair projection lemma, with the projection mate fixed canonically as the adjoint transpose of tensor(unit,identity) followed by the inverse restriction comparison, the displayed chain comparison equation holds for a cochain C and P with P K-flat and flat terms.
statement_change.what: The previous statement allowed arbitrary one-flat comparison families. Changing only the ambient component by postcomposition with a nontrivial automorphism preserves every listed hypothesis, changes the right side and leaves the left side fixed. Add agreement with the simultaneous models and the flat-term K-flat hypotheses on C already present in the sole caller. This restores the resolving-pair statement intended in the parent; it is a statement repair, not a proof of the former false statement.

citers.note: Already assumes ambientBoth, openBoth, hC and flatC. Its proof is adapted to pass these arguments; its statement is unchanged.

old_proof.text: On each signed total summand, use D.ordinaryInverse, hordinary, and the summand formulas to identify the adjunct of the chain map with the tensor of the adjunction unit and identity followed by the inverse restriction comparison.
Localize the chain equality through the exact derived adjunction and substitute the supplied one-flat comparison models.
